notes.title: Raji: An Ancient Epic Update “Developers vs Code Demons!”
notes.content:
[h3]Good news everyone,[/h3]

Since the launch of the game, we’ve been closely monitoring the various issues that you in our community have been reporting to us. Needless to say, all of the bugs that have been reported to us have been noted and passed to our developers to fix up, and now, we’re ready to announce the first update to Raji: An Ancient Epic!
[h3]
Developers vs Code Demons - The Patchnotes![/h3]
Before we begin, we just want to make clear that this update focuses entirely on bugfixes and so is designed to improve the general quality of life for all of our players.

[b]So, what have we fixed?[/b]

[h3]Frame-rate/FPS Related Issues[/h3]
There were two major locations in the game where the game was almost unplayable if the player was on a high-end system (and so had high frames per second), these were:
[list]
[*] 
[*] When Raji had to pull the rope down from the giant bow
[*] When Raji encountered the Naga and needed to use stealth to avoid it.
[/list]
This bug has now been fixed, so if you have manually put in a frame rate cap via the GameUserSettings.ini file, or via any third-party software, you may now remove it and play the game with the maximum performance that your hardware allows.

[h3]Raji Gets Stuck[/h3]
One of the main pain-points that our community highlighted was that there are several locations where, if Raji tried to move on/around, would result in the character getting stuck, requiring a restart from your last save point. The stuck locations that we have fixed are:

During the sequence where Raji sees the giant bow and has to run a gauntlet while the terrain crumbled, it was possible for Raji to get stuck on the cliffs, with no option other than to fall.
A general issue (across all levels) caused Raji to sometimes get stuck in the floor, most commonly encountered after crossing the first bridge in the first level.

We do hope that the fixes for these issues will mean that Raji will no longer get stuck in all locations as you play the game.

[h3]Tutorial Mission for the Bow[/h3]
Soon after unlocking the bow, a tutorial mission is triggered and the player needs to complete a set of combos. However, many players would swap to the Trishul and attempt to complete the tutorial with the Trishul, not knowing that the Bow is required. To fix this, when the tutorial starts, Raji will automatically swap weapons to the Bow.

[h3]Quality of Life/Game Experience Fixes and Changes[/h3]
All of these points are important, however, do not follow a specific theme, so they’re listed here.
[list]
[*] Sometimes Raji would not jump far enough to reach a wall run section,
[*] In rare instances, jumping on a Lotus would cause Raji to die,
[*] Steam Achievements would either take far too long to update or in rare cases, not update at all.
[*] When loading the game (or reviving) from specific checkpoints, the start position was in an awkward place preventing Raji from being able to move.
[*] The colour scheme of the red wall in the temple has been slightly altered, making it easier for the player to know where to go.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

We’d like to thank everyone in our community for reporting the bugs to us, it really is with your help that we were able to identify and fix these issues. As always, after updating the game, please continue to report any new and/or old bugs to us as we are constantly working on improving the game.

Thank you very much,
Your Raji Team!

notes.title: Important Update to Raji: An Ancient Epic
notes.content:
[h3]Good afternoon everyone,[/h3]

Launch week has flown by us and it’s been a really amazing experience to watch people from all over the world come together and enjoy Raji: An Ancient Epic!

We also noticed something really special from this community that we want to highlight. Simply put, the level of support that you have shown us-and-each other, and the way that you all have banded together to help bring awareness of the game to all corners of the internet has been frankly amazing. So, a huge thank you to everyone!

[h3]Post Launch Issues and Fixes[/h3]
One thing that every game ever launched will have are a few nagging issues that are only picked up on after the game’s launch. 

Why’s that you may ask? Surely we tested everything, so how did this happen?

The reason for this is down to the huge variance that exists from each PC set up. Take our studio for example, even between us where we use similar systems, what our Game Designer, Avichal Singh uses is different from what our Game Artists Ian Maude and Shruti Ghosh use, and it’s not just the hardware, it’s the software configuration. Now think about the countless number of people playing Raji and the hardware and software combinations will explode. From our side, we tested the game with over 40 different hardware and software configurations that covered the most popular specifications to ensure that everything was working well. With that said, we were always on standby in case unforeseen issues came up - and so we were ready to act when we began receiving reports from our community. 

A huge thanks to our Game Programmers who have been hyper-focused on an update to Raji - one that we just pushed live now!

[h3]The Update - Listening to the Community[/h3]
Our update covers two main points. The first is straight forward, we realized that there was an interesting exploit that allowed players to defeat the Chieftain very easily, the frustrating thing about this was that players could accidentally come across it and so would have their gaming experience somewhat damaged as the fight would become very anticlimactic, so we’re happy to have this bug fixed and we hope that you will be as well.

The second point is perhaps more important to a rather large group in our community, and that is the DRM. To give it to you short, this update has removed the DRM from our game, and so any bugs that are related to the DRM will vanish.

The point of DRM is always a very sensitive topic for gamers. On one hand, DRM can be vital to developers as it slows down (never stops) the more unscrupulous types from pirating the game. However, even the best of DRM will have its issues, sometimes it can block honest players who have done nothing wrong, or sometimes it can harm the game’s performance. That said, we want to be clear that our DRM did not impact performance, something we are very proud of.

With that said, looking at the feedback of our community, we saw that there were too many players that had purchased the game and were unable to play it - an unacceptable situation to everyone who works on the game. Then, we also had the players that for personal reasons extremely dislike DRM due to the reputation and nature of it, something that we have nothing against at all, after all, we are gamers at heart as well and can understand some of the sentiments behind it.

So, after listening to what our community has had to say, and after doing our best to try to help the innocent - but affected players - we made the decision (today) to remove the DRM from our game with this update. All you need to do is update the game and it will be gone.

Anyone that has had a problem with ‘[Cord] Game load failed’ should now be able to play.

[h3]Looking to the Future[/h3]
We know that this update is a rather small one, however especially with the DRM issue, we are sure that you will all agree that this was a vital update. There are more things that need working and there are some other bugs that need squashing, so rest assured that we are now preparing work on a much larger update - but one that will take a bit longer to put together.

notes.title: Meet the team - Shruti Ghosh, Co-Founder and Game Artist
notes.content:
[h2]Hello everyone,[/h2]

In just over two weeks (October 15) Raji: An Ancient Epic will finally launch on Steam and we hope that you are just as excited for the launch as we are!

As the launch is just around the corner we want to give you a look at the team behind the game, starting with our amazing co-founder and game artist, Shruti Ghosh. 

So, Shruti very kindly put aside some time to talk about her experiences and answer a few questions about her journey so far!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

[h3]Can you tell us how your journey with the Nodding Heads Team started?[/h3]
It started back in college, Ian and I (Ian is another Nodding Heads Team co-founder and artist) were game art lecturers and we met Avichal who at the time was in his final year of studies.

Back then, Avichal and I were both big fans of Bastion and Transistor and we both had the vision to create a game that represents India on the global market, what's more, Avichal was (and still is) greatly inspired by the architecture of Rajasthan, which linked very well to my love of the old traditional arts of India. After we got to know each other more we began to talk about our aspirations to make a game, this was the start of the Raji project!

That said, we didn't things start right away as we always chipped away at the concept of Raji bit by bit. On my side, I drew some sketches that we then showed to our closest friends and asked them if they would be interested in playing a game set in the universe that we were making, the response was absolutely positive which really helped us push forward.

Eventually, in 2016 we left our jobs and started to work on Raji's prototype, from there, the rest is history!

[i]Our next question tackles Shruti's preferred style of drawing![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

[h3]What painting style do you like using the most, and what style did you use for Raji the most?[/h3]
I love the Pahari / miniature paintings and Madhubani paintings. These paintings are so intricate, the use of color is magnificent, and the amount of detail in these small paintings is insane. They literally paint thousands of leaves on the trees and gold details on the jewelry and clothes of the kings and queens. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/8f4878af01e598e2bae8b7e30ec17f1296f1bf7a.png[/img]

This form of art or mostly all traditional art forms of India are slowly diminishing hence Raji’s art style was a nod or tribute to this great art form. I wanted to capture the old worn out faded paintings on walls of palaces and temples which tell thousand-year-old stories in the paintings of Raji.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/243b4ae04f16821dbc0f344bbb0aed8548126b0c.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

[i]Contining with the art theme, we were curious about how long it took Shruti to complete a typical scene in Raji: An Ancient Epic[/i]

[h3]How long did it take you to draw a typical scene in Raji?[/h3]
It's hard to say as art is a team effort, so any piece will be worked on by many people!
The concept art is done by Anirudh, the entire environment which you see throughout the game is mostly made by me and Shreyas, though Ian and Jalay contributed as well. 

However, for the gods and goddesses avatar paintings, the line art was made by Anirudh and then it would take me roughly an hour (or more) to paint them, usually, it is a time-consuming process.

I remember the longest panel that I drew was the Durga blessing where it is blessed with all the weapons by different gods, that took quite a while as it was a huge panel.

That said I thoroughly enjoyed it and it was one of my favorite pieces to work on!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

[i]Continuing on the theme of favorites [/i]

[h3]What was your favorite drawing (for Raji) that you worked on?[/h3]
I've never really thought about that! 
The Durga blessing from the first level (as I mentioned in the last question) and probably the mandala of Golu’s birth would probably be my favorite as I just love the composition of it all! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/71008fecf2b36308e04eb920cfe6ac90a1adc689.jpg[/img]

Ani did a stellar job in visualizing it and I just added colors and a bit of life to it. It was a team effort between me and Anirudh and I love the final results.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

[i]More on the art but now looking on the challenges[/i]

[h3]What was the most challenging drawing that you had to tackle?[/h3]
Honestly, it was all challenging as I knew that I only had limited time to complete the paintings and there were so many panels for each level. But I think that the third level story of Garuda had the most number of panels. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/778cdb33dc7125395a94c0e43e9db21fd5398270.jpg[/img]

That piece took a lot of time and some parts were really small and had quite a bit of detail in it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

[i]Now we move to more personal topics about Shruti and how she got into art[/i]

[h3]What was it that made you want to become an artist?[/h3]
I think it was a natural choice for me. Quite early on my parents knew that Iw ould choose a career in art! My mom would always tell the story of how, when I was young, I would pick up the newspaper ads or pictures and then try to draw them myself!

I was the happiest the day they sent to learn art in a drawing school, and that was the moment that I had the biggest smile. 

But choosing game art happened accidentally as I wanted to be more of a traditional artist. I love paints, paper, and pencils more than computers. But in the end, it worked out nicely!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

[i]Looking into Shruti's journey into art, we wanted to know more about her inspirations[/i]

[h3]What were your sources of inspiration for both private art and Raji related art?[/h3]
Generally, I am inspired by a lot of things in life with nature being my biggest inspiration as I feel the calmest amidst trees and greenery, however, architecture also plays an important role in inspiring me creatively. 

To me, India is such a vast canvas of art as every state has its own art form and history to go with it, any artist would be inspired by that. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/6ab97d50fcf4965c7bc56e084ed93474e73a543f.png[/img]

For Raji, primarily it was the palaces and forts of Rajasthan that were the major inspiration sources, then there were also the Pahari paintings, and the Balinese mythology and culture for imagining the entire universe and style for the asura clans. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/8e065f3a95771a898117e270ad176af529c159ff.jpg[/img]

Also, our cutscenes draw inspiration from Wayang puppet shows and shadow puppetry which is used in a few parts of India to tell mythological tales. I remember that when I was a child in Bengal, outside a temple they used to tell tales of Lord Krishna and Ram, I used to love listening to them as a kid, and even now thinking about them still gives me just joy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

[i]Bringing everything together in a nice circle, we looped back to the experience of developing Raji: An Ancient Epic[/i]

[h3]Many of us know about the roller-coaster ride that accompanied the development of Raji: An Ancient Epic. Did this affect what you drew for the game? And if it did, what part of the game would you really love to re-do?[/h3]

That’s a really good and tough question. I guess the ups and downs did affect all of us in the company, and even more so for Avichal, Ian, and I, as we had the added responsibilities of running the company and making sure that everybody was paid.

Sometimes the pressure of running it all did get to me, things like running the day to day affair of the company (which wasn't easy to do) and then the daily task of making art for the game would quickly pile on. There were times that I didn't feel like painting or making an asset for a level because my mind wasn't cooperating, but I still had to do it because we were in a race against time. 

I think that if we didn't have to spend six months struggling to find funding and we could have concentrated on the production of the game instead, we could have done a lot more to the art or overall game, and I could have painted more details on those avatar paintings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

[i]Looking to the post-launch days, we were curious to know what Shruti had planned[/i]

[h3]With the launch of the game less than a month away, what are you planning to do once that happens?[/h3]
Take a break definitely! We hardly spent any time with our dogs during the last year, so we want to take them for some outdoor activities or take them for a trip somewhere. I am also planning to do a few art courses from the London School of Arts so I am excited about them.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

[i]And to end things, a special question to help the budding artists out there![/i]

[h3]There are many people that have been inspired to draw after seeing the art in Raji: An Ancient Epic, do you have any tips for those that are just starting out?[/h3]
We love seeing different artists depicting Raji in their own art style! It’s really humbling to see all of the art and love that everyone is pouring into Raji. 

My advice is, don't think about what you can do or can't, always keep practicing, trying new stuff, and never stop learning!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/fc11269959d5bc9e2150e6b8c22347be157bf4ad.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/7e925db8c1be94d127ee06075485587b98a8f547.jpg[/img]

notes.content:
[h1]2019 Indie DB Players Choice [/h1]
The 2019 IndieDB player's choice best upcoming indie game results are in and thanks to your help, from 100 awesome games, Raji came in third!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/8603115c315dff4d5d6823ef533b73e909cd93e4.png[/img]

That is a fantastic result and we are extremely grateful to everyone who voted for us!

[h1]Raji in the Newspaper[/h1]
The Times of India, one of the biggest newspapers in India, recently wrote an article about Indian game developers and how they have begun to grab the attention of people from around the world. 

Whatsmore, in the article, we were honored to be recognized as being instrumental in helping the Indian Gaming industry receive global attention!

Check out what they had to say about us and the ever-growing Indian game developer scene!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/34c7302ae84aaebefdd4c5455bb1d775f641e4dd.jpg[/img]

[h1]Steam Demo[/h1]
As you may know, for a while we have had a playable demo of our game on Steam. 
 
However, this demo was created for our Kickstarter campaign making it over two years old and in that time we have pretty much re-worked the entire game making the demo extremely outdated. 

Whatsmore, we have noticed that this has caused some confusion in our community as players have been judging the game based on this outdated demo - something that we really do not want to happen.

So to prevent our new community members from getting confused, we have decided to remove our steam demo. If you already have the demo, nothing will happen (you can manually delete it if you want), however, new members of the community will not be able to download the old demo.

If you are interested in seeing just how different the game is, check out this video that compares the scene where Raji receives her first weapon, the Trishul.

[previewyoutube=BtwgEmIF_7s;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Game Development - Movement Leads to Combat[/h1]
Shortly after releasing our Kickstarter demo (two years ago) we received a lot of feedback from players who commented that Raji’s movement felt clunky and repetitive.

After studying what the players wrote, we agreed with the conclusion and set to work on improving this. We did this by taking up a new mindset that we called ‘Movement leads to combat’.

One of the first things that we implemented after adopting this mindset was the triple dodge mechanic that you can see in this video.

Notice how Raji has three different moves and each one flows seamlessly from one to the next.

[previewyoutube=N2frXdB6SQU;full][/previewyoutube]

It’s time for the Raji weekly news blast, bringing you up to date with all of the latest from the team!

[b]IndieDB is looking for the best Indie Game of 2019[/b]
Let’s start with something interesting! We have had a long and proud history with IndieDB with many people originally finding out about us when we were featured on the site.

IndieDB is currently looking for the best Indie Game of 2019, how does this relate to us, as we have not yet released? Well, by the rules of the competition active, as of yet unreleased indie games (like Raji: An Ancient Epic) are eligible to win in the “best upcoming” categories!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/1232cfc709644ef0b11c8d988761ab8a6ed007ed.jpg[/img]

So, is Raji the game that you are looking forward to the most, the game that you feel is the best upcoming game? If so, please do vote for us over on our [url=https://www.indiedb.com/games/raji-an-ancient-epic]IndieDB page[/url]

[h1]Get Indie Gaming - Top 10 Upcoming Games[/h1]
If you have not already seen this video, then we highly recommend that you watch it now!

Get Indie Gaming, a very popular YouTube channel for indie games has identified Raji: An Ancient Epic as one of their top 10 upcoming games for 2020!

[previewyoutube=6qTz3EJw6Hs;full][/previewyoutube]

Be sure to check the video out as they also talk about a host of other games that are extremely interesting!

[h1]Vayusra Combat[/h1]
You may have seen the flying Vayusra demon a few times now, but have you seen it in combat?

While testing out one of the future levels that we’re currently working on, we had to fight our way through these flying terrors. Check out how that went in this week’s work-in-progress video.

[previewyoutube=sZZglJTJ0hc;full][/previewyoutube]

That’s it for this news blast, we hope that you’re just as excited for the game as we are!

notes.title: Raji News Blast - Winning Awards at Dev Play 2019!
notes.content:
Hello and welcome to this week’s special news blast!

[h1]Dev Play 2019[/h1]
We’ve got some fantastic news coming from Bucharest, Romania!  

Last week, between November 7th - 8th, the Game Dev Conference for Eastern Europe, aka Dev Play, was held. During this event, our game (Raji: An Ancient Epic) won awards for:
[list]
[*] The Best Game Design
[*] The Best Game of the Show
[*] The Best Visuals
[/list]

To win these three awards is a feeling that is hard to describe, but needless to say that we are ecstatic to see our game get this sort of recognition!

In our last news blast, we introduced Blocktober to you, telling you what it was, and why we're taking part as well. If you haven't read the post yet, we do recommend that you check it out [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/730390/announcements/detail/1586880891240019487]first[/url].

The first looks at the before and after of the first Wall Run that Raji is forced to perform.

The second video looks at combat. Notice how in the blocking phase, we had already planned for the tutorial by making notes on the ground itself.

[previewyoutube=KhXW98bCxf8;full][/previewyoutube]

Meet the Raji team dogs! These dogs are one of the main reasons why we've managed to maintain our sanity while developing Raji: An Ancient Epic!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/58331d70cb118c9cf929b1b57c64831c0654ea71.png[/img]

From the mouth of the Raji team, the dogs in the photo are:
[i]Killer is in the mix three times... cheeky chappy. 
From top left, we have Benji, little Patch, Killer, 
Left middle row, Hailey [the Alpha], Zia [Killers sister] and Peter, 
Bottom left, Killer, Killer again and then we finish with Nimi. 

We're missing Mr G. Goldie. Each one has their own story, Nimi was only meant to stay with us until her leg healed - she was hit by a car, we'll spare you the details. Once she was fit and well, it was I who said, I can't let her go, Normally it's Shru.

notes.title: Raji: An Ancient Epic - Post Event!
notes.content:
The last few weeks have been quite eventful filled with convention goodness, from Gamescom in Germany, to ID@Xbox and the MIX in the United States. A great time was had by all, and we’ll be doing a few more write-ups about all of the events soon, so stay tuned!

In the meantime, as it’s been a while, we’ll give a quick overview of what we’ve been working on and sharing!

[h1]Voice Acting[/h1]
Voice acting is a major part of game development, while graphics provide the eye-candy, a good voice actor provides the ear-candy!

We made sure to take a few snaps and record a few videos from a recent voice acting session where our own Shru was recording for Durga, with Avichal handling the tech side of things.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/8b548bee7883be11ce0a7711c623a96c20c1adba.png[/img]

Check out this video if you want to hear some quick clips!

[previewyoutube=FgxgHnLi-SU;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]The Demonic Tree[/h1]
On our various social media channels, we revealed a pretty big new part of the game - a demonic tree.

We initially started with the concept art, asking the community whether or not they had an idea what the tree represents. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30912759/cb24ff9ffca6776bda5f8834d4ca48df6e6d7b07.jpg[/img]

Though our community had a bunch of pretty awesome ideas, none was exactly correct. The demon tree will only appear in an area corrupted by demonic energies. However, the level of corruption needed to spawn a demon tree can only be achieved under one very specific condition - a condition that we’re keeping secret for now!

Can you guess what could cause this tree to spawn?

While you think about the tree, we’d like to also share what exactly the tree looks like, so sit back and enjoy this short video clip!

[previewyoutube=EPWmUVJZ2oE;full][/previewyoutube]

And that's it for now, we hope that you've enjoyed this quick round up. We'll be back soon with our event write up!

notes.title: Raji: An Ancient Epic Summer News Blast volume 3
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30912759/97a8e6e3ba0ac3477677e703cbac0a307b86d147.png[/img]

The Raji weekly digest is coming to you on Monday this time round!

For this week’s edition, three different demons are taking center stage. 
They are: 
The mighty Gadasura 
The agile Mahinasura
The acidic Tezabsura.

As always, we highly recommend that you follow us on our Social Media channels as we upload new content there on a regular basis.

[b]Our full social media list is:[/b]
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/rajithegame
Twitter: https://twitter.com/rajithegame
Instagram: https://instagram.com/rajithegame/
VK (Russian only): https://vk.com/rajithegame

[h1]The Demons[/h1]
If you’ve played our demo you’ll recognize these demons as they are the enemies that you have to fight your way through.

[b]The Gadasura[/b]
This is the mighty Gadasura demon. When you encounter it be sure to avoid its club as it will make quick work of anyone on the receiving end. 

A common way for it to attack you is to first charge at you with surprising speed while swinging its powerful club.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ov5WtEkOnmQ 

[b]The Mahinasura[/b]
The Mahinasura is the opposite of the Gadasura, while the former relies on brute force, the Mahinasura relies on crafty tactics and agility. It will run into battle, attack a few times, and then quickly retreat to a safe distance.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NrIZAHCmG7g 

[b]The Tezabsura[/b]
The Tezabsura poses an entirely different challenge to the previous two demons. This demon has three distinct attacks. 

If Raji gets noticed, it will hurl balls of acid at her, if Raji gets very close, it will use its powerful hind legs to knock Raji to the ground and leap to safety. Once Raji finally defeats the Tezabsura, it will swell up and self destruct, burning everything around it.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J3Uz2uh65u4 

As this news blast is a bit shorter, we've got a bonus video for you!
Check out the Tezabsura’s ranged attack and defensive kick:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4RbCO7y1cvo

notes.title: Raji: An Ancient Epic, the road ahead
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30912759/3f4c6b51d93eaaec082fa42ee794508efeac4581.png[/img]

Hello everyone,

It's been quite a while since we last gave you an update, and though things have been quite we have always been hard at work working on Raji: An Ancient Epic.

[b]The Story So Far[/b]
As you may know, the creating Raji: An Ancient Epic has been quite a wild rollercoaster ride, and though we struggled for two years, our perseverance paid off and we are on track for a Q1 2020 release.

[b]Working with a dedicated publisher[/b]
We are really pleased to announce that in preparation for our launch next year, we have partnered up with super.com, who will be the dedicated publisher for Raji. You will be hearing a lot more from us, so be sure to follow us on our social media channels:

[/list]

And of course, we will be publishing news directly to Steam to keep you hyped and interested!

[b]GDC Trailer[/b]
To kick things off, we'd like to present you an all-new trailer, made exclusively for GDC!
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CKYU_bcf_VA

[b]Coming soon, a new demo[/b]
That's not all, the most exciting announcement is yet to come!

We have come a long way since we first released our demo and since then we have been hard at work improving pretty much every aspect of the game, focus heavily on the story and gameplay. Though it is early days, we aim to have this new and improved demo ready for you to play later this year.
